images.alt_grc: ὁ Περικλῆς ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος πρὸς τὸν δῆμον λέγει.
images.alt_en: Winter 431/430 BC, the public cemetery outside the Dipylon Gate: Pericles, bearded, helmet pushed back, speaks from a high wooden platform; below him ten cypress coffins and a crowd of citizens, foreigners and women in mourning.

images.alt_grc: ὁ αὐτὸς ἀνὴρ καὶ κεραμεύς ἐστι καὶ πολίτης.
images.alt_en: Two halves of one picture: on the left an Athenian potter at his wheel in a simple workshop; on the right the same man on the Pnyx, raising his hand to vote among other citizens.

images.alt_grc: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι καὶ τολμῶσι καὶ λογίζονται.
images.alt_en: Athenian hoplites and rowers setting out from Piraeus at dawn, a general in front of them pointing at a map scratched on a wax tablet: daring and calculation together.
The Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens, west or east façade, in clear light (temple built 447–438 BC, sculpture completed 432 BC).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κλέων ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ βοᾷ.
images.alt_en: The Pnyx in 427 BC: Cleon, a loud, gesturing speaker without a cloak thrown properly over his shoulder, shouting from the platform; citizens raising hands to vote; in the distance a single trireme leaving Piraeus.
The next day on the Pnyx: a calm speaker, Diodotus, answers; the crowd is split, hands raised on both sides, a herald counting.
Inside a trireme at night: rowers pulling at their oars while eating barley mixed with wine and oil from bowls; others asleep on the benches, taking turns; a lamp at the stern.
The Olympias, a full-size reconstruction of an Athenian trireme (1987), under oars in the Saronic Gulf or moored at Faliro.

images.alt_grc: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐν Σικελίᾳ πεζοὶ ἀποχωροῦσιν.
images.alt_en: Sicily, September 413 BC: a long, exhausted column of Athenian hoplites and unarmed men marching inland over dry hills, wounded carried on shoulders; far behind, burnt-out triremes on the shore of the Great Harbour of Syracuse.
Syracusan horsemen and javelin-throwers attacking the retreating column from every side; Nicias, a sick older general, riding in the middle of his men at dawn.

images.alt_grc: οἱ Ἀθηναῖοι ἐν τῷ ποταμῷ πίνουσιν.
images.alt_en: The river Assinarus: a narrow stream in a steep ravine choked with men and shields; men drinking the muddy water; Syracusans shooting from the high bank above. No gore; the horror shown by the crowd and the bank.
The ancient stone quarries of Syracuse (Latomia del Paradiso, with the cave called the 'Ear of Dionysius'), where the Athenian prisoners were held in 413 BC.

images.alt_grc: αἱ τῶν Ἀθηναίων νῆες ἐν Αἰγὸς ποταμοῖς ὁρμοῦσιν.
images.alt_en: The Hellespont in late summer 405 BC, seen from above like a map: on the European shore the open beach of Aegospotami with some 180 Athenian triremes pulled up, the crews wandering inland; across the strait the town of Lampsacus and Lysander's fleet in its harbour; a small scout ship halfway across.

Mid-strait, a scout ship's crewman raises a bronze shield that flashes in the sun; behind it Lysander's triremes surge across at full speed; on the far beach Conon, a general in a red cloak, signals frantically to men running back to half-empty ships.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Πάραλος εἰς τὰς Ἀθήνας ἀποπλεῖ.
images.alt_en: A handful of fully manned triremes breaking away to the south, one flying a sacred pennant (the Paralus); on the beach behind, Spartan soldiers rounding up Athenian sailors beside captured, empty ships.
A hoplite's round bronze-faced shield (aspis), seen from the front and the inside with its arm-band and hand-grip.
The Athlit ram: a bronze warship ram of about 200 BC found off the coast of Israel (National Maritime Museum, Haifa), showing the three horizontal cutting blades.

images.alt_grc: νυκτὸς οἰμωγὴ διὰ τῶν μακρῶν τειχῶν διήκει.
images.alt_en: Night in Athens, 405 BC: torches along the Long Walls between Piraeus and the city; people coming out of their houses, women lamenting, a man running up the road between the walls with the news; in the harbour a single trireme with a sacred pennant.
Spring 404 BC at the city gate: thin, hungry Athenians crowding round a returning embassy led by Theramenes, a well-dressed man raising a hand to calm them.

Peloponnesian soldiers and returned exiles pulling down a stretch of the Long Walls with crowbars and ropes while flute-girls play the double pipes; Spartan ships sailing into Piraeus in the background.

images.alt_grc: τὸ Θεμιστόκλειον τεῖχος ἐν τῷ Κεραμεικῷ.
images.alt_en: The excavated remains of the Themistoclean city wall and the Dipylon Gate in the Kerameikos, Athens: stone socle courses with the later mudbrick removed.
